rationale: Intra-ampullary papillary-tubular neoplasm (IAPN) is defined as a tumoral intraepithelial neoplasm arising within the ampulla of Vater; population analyses filter it exclusively to C24.1. The code's SMVL ceiling also includes biliary, pancreas and breast sites, so the term is restricted to a proper subset (ampulla).
source_name: Med Sci Monit - IAPN population-based analysis (ICD-O-3 site C24.1)

rationale: WHO 5th ed and large series establish goblet cell adenocarcinoma occurs almost exclusively in the appendix (90.5% appendiceal in a national series); true extra-appendiceal cases are exceedingly rare and likely occult appendiceal primaries. This restricts it to a proper subset of the code's intestinal-tract SMVL sites.
source_name: Frontiers in Oncology - Goblet Cell Adenocarcinoma of the Appendix: Systematic Review

rationale: Goblet cell carcinoid (the former name of goblet cell adenocarcinoma) arises almost exclusively in the appendix, with rare cases outside this location; true extra-appendiceal disease requires excluding an occult appendiceal primary. This restricts it to a proper subset of the code's intestinal-tract SMVL sites.
source_name: World J Gastrointest Oncol - Goblet cell carcinoid tumors of the appendix: overview

rationale: Goblet cell carcinoma/adenocarcinoma is an amphicrine appendiceal neoplasm occurring almost exclusively in the appendix per WHO 5th ed; extra-appendiceal presentations are exceedingly rare and likely represent occult appendiceal primaries. This restricts it to a proper subset of the code's intestinal-tract SMVL sites.
source_name: Frontiers in Oncology - Goblet Cell Adenocarcinoma of the Appendix: Systematic Review

term: Pancreatic peptide and pancreatic peptide-like peptide within terminal tyrosine amide producing tumor
rationale: Pancreatic-polypeptide-producing tumors (PPomas) are predominantly pancreatic (islet-cell); the code's ceiling additionally includes the colon/rectum, so the literature-dominant pancreatic usage is a strict subset.
source_name: PubMed Central - PPoma review

rationale: Acinar adenocarcinoma (8551/3) is explicitly a lung-only entity in the WHO/IASLC lung classification (SEER and FCDS materials note 8551 is 'lung only'). The code's SMVL ceiling also includes pancreas, thyroid and other sites, so this named term is restricted to the lung subset.
source_name: FCDS 2023 Lung and Thorax Neoplasms WHO 5th ed (8551/3 - Lung Only)

rationale: Acinar cell cystadenocarcinoma is a rare malignant epithelial neoplasm of the pancreas (cystic acinar-differentiated tumor with exocrine enzyme production). The code's SMVL ceiling also includes lung, thyroid and other sites, so this term is restricted to the pancreatic subset.
source_name: Case Rep Gastroenterol - Acinar Cell Cystadenocarcinoma of the Pancreas

rationale: Undifferentiated (embryonal) sarcoma of the liver is a hepatic mesenchymal tumor arising in the liver. The code's SMVL ceiling also includes peritoneum/retroperitoneum, penis, eye/orbit and other sites, so this named term is restricted to the liver.
source_name: PMC - Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver: a rare hepatic tumor

rationale: Undifferentiated (embryonal) sarcoma of the liver is a hepatic mesenchymal tumor arising in the liver. The code's SMVL ceiling also includes peritoneum/retroperitoneum, penis, eye/orbit and other sites, so this named term is restricted to the liver.
source_name: PMC - Undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma of the liver: a rare hepatic tumor

rationale: Calcitonin-secreting (calcitoninoma) functioning NETs are pancreatic-origin tumours; ENETS covers these functioning syndromes with the primary tumour originating in the pancreas. Restricting to the pancreatic codes excludes the ampulla-of-Vater code (C241) that is also in the ceiling, so it is a proper subset.
source_name: ENETS 2023 guidance paper for functioning pancreatic NET syndromes (J Neuroendocrinol)

rationale: CCK-producing functioning NET is a pancreatic NET among the rare functioning pancreatic syndromes; confining to pancreatic codes excludes the ampulla (C241) in the ceiling, making it a proper subset.
source_name: ENETS 2023 guidance paper for functioning pancreatic NET syndromes (J Neuroendocrinol)

rationale: CRH/ACTH-producing functioning NETs of this class are pancreatic-origin tumours (pancreatic NETs), so confining usage to the pancreatic codes excludes the ampulla-of-Vater code (C241) in the ceiling, forming a proper subset.
source_name: Ann Hepatobiliary Pancreat Surg (PMC5353908): ACTH-producing neuroendocrine tumor of the pancreas

rationale: An erythropoietin-producing functioning NET of this group is a pancreatic NET; restricting to the pancreatic codes excludes the ampulla (C241) in the ceiling, so it occupies a proper subset.
source_name: ENETS 2023 guidance paper for functioning pancreatic NET syndromes (J Neuroendocrinol)

rationale: Ghrelin-producing functioning NET (pancreatic ghrelinoma) is a pancreatic-origin tumour; confining to pancreatic codes excludes the ceiling's ampulla code (C241), making it a proper subset.

rationale: GHRH-producing functioning NETs of this type arise in the pancreas (pancreatic NETs causing ectopic acromegaly); restricting to pancreatic codes excludes the ampulla (C241) in the ceiling, so it forms a proper subset.
source_name: Neupsy Key: Pancreatic NETs producing GHRH, GH, ghrelin, PTH or PTHrP

rationale: PTH/PTHrP-producing functioning NETs (PTHrPoma) are pancreatic-origin tumours; confining to the pancreatic codes excludes the ceiling's ampulla-of-Vater code (C241), making it a proper subset.
source_name: ENETS 2023 guidance paper for functioning pancreatic NET syndromes (J Neuroendocrinol)

rationale: A vasopressin-producing functioning NET of this group is a pancreatic NET; restricting to the pancreatic codes excludes the ampulla (C241) in the ceiling, so its real usage is a proper subset.
source_name: ENETS 2023 guidance paper for functioning pancreatic NET syndromes (J Neuroendocrinol)

rationale: Mixed (ductal-)acinar cell carcinoma is a pancreatic exocrine neoplasm defined by coexisting acinar and ductal components within a pancreatic tumour; confining usage to the pancreatic codes excludes the prostate code (C619) that is also in the ceiling, so it is a proper subset.
source_name: Mol Clin Oncol (PMC6449909): Mixed ductal-acinar cell carcinoma of the pancreas

rationale: Bile duct adenocarcinoma arises from the bile-duct epithelium (intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree); gallbladder cancer is classified as a separate biliary tract cancer, so bile-duct adenocarcinoma excludes the gallbladder code (C239) in the ceiling and occupies a proper subset.
source_name: Wikipedia: Cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer; gallbladder cancer is a separate biliary tract cancer)

rationale: Bile duct carcinoma is cancer of the bile-duct epithelium throughout the intra/extrahepatic biliary tree; because gallbladder cancer is a distinct biliary tract entity, the term excludes the gallbladder code (C239) in the ceiling and therefore occupies a proper subset.
source_name: Wikipedia: Cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer; gallbladder cancer is a separate biliary tract cancer)

rationale: WHO 5th ed uses 'carcinoma of extrahepatic bile ducts' specifically for tumors arising in the extrahepatic biliary tree, distinct from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and gallbladder carcinoma. This restricts the term to the extrahepatic bile duct subset of the code's biliary SMVL sites.
source_name: PMC - Pathology of Cholangiocarcinoma (WHO: carcinoma of extrahepatic bile ducts)

term: Carcinoma of the extrahepatics bile ducts
rationale: This is the WHO term for carcinoma arising in the extrahepatic bile ducts (a typographic variant of 'carcinoma of the extrahepatic bile ducts'), distinct from intrahepatic and gallbladder carcinoma. It restricts to the extrahepatic bile duct subset of the code's biliary SMVL sites.
source_name: PMC - Pathology of Cholangiocarcinoma (WHO: carcinoma of extrahepatic bile ducts)

rationale: Cholangiocarcinoma is bile-duct cancer arising anywhere along the bile ducts (intrahepatic, perihilar, distal/extrahepatic); gallbladder cancer is explicitly a separate biliary tract cancer, so cholangiocarcinoma excludes the gallbladder code (C239) in the ceiling and is a proper subset.
source_name: Wikipedia: Cholangiocarcinoma (intrahepatic/perihilar/distal bile ducts; gallbladder cancer separate)

rationale: The large-duct type is a WHO 5th ed histological subtype specific to intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (arising from large intrahepatic ducts near the hilum). This restricts the term to the intrahepatic bile duct subset of the code's biliary SMVL sites.
source_name: Cancers - Recent Advances in Pathology of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma (WHO 5th ed small/large duct)

rationale: The small-duct type is a WHO 5th ed histological subtype specific to intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (peripheral, arising from small intrahepatic ducts). This restricts the term to the intrahepatic bile duct subset of the code's biliary SMVL sites.
source_name: Cancers - Recent Advances in Pathology of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma (WHO 5th ed small/large duct)

rationale: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma by definition arises within the intrahepatic biliary tree; WHO 5th ed reserves this term for the intrahepatic ducts, distinct from extrahepatic and gallbladder carcinoma. This restricts it to the intrahepatic bile duct subset of the code's biliary SMVL sites.
source_name: Cancers - Recent Advances in Pathology of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma

rationale: Large-duct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is a WHO 5th ed subtype arising from large intrahepatic bile ducts near the hilum; by definition it is intrahepatic, restricting it to the intrahepatic bile duct subset of the code's biliary SMVL sites.
source_name: Cancers - Recent Advances in Pathology of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma (WHO 5th ed small/large duct)

rationale: Small-duct intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is a WHO 5th ed subtype arising peripherally from small intrahepatic bile ducts; by definition it is intrahepatic, restricting it to the intrahepatic bile duct subset of the code's biliary SMVL sites.
source_name: Cancers - Recent Advances in Pathology of Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma (WHO 5th ed small/large duct)

rationale: Anal gland/duct adenocarcinoma originates from the anal glands and ducts and is centred in the anal canal wall (between anal margin and ~2 cm above the dentate line); this localises it to the anal canal (C211), a proper subset of the four-code ceiling (which also includes anus NOS, cloacogenic zone and anorectal-overlapping).

rationale: Anal gland adenocarcinoma is an extramucosal adenocarcinoma arising from the anal glands/ducts, which lie within the wall of the anal canal and open near the dentate line; it is restricted to the anal canal rather than the full code ceiling (anus NOS/anal margin, cloacogenic zone, anorectum-overlapping).

rationale: Teratoid medulloepithelioma is an embryonal neuroepithelial tumor of the CNS/neural-tube derivatives (and eye, which is outside this ceiling); within this ceiling it maps to ventricular/cerebellar/brainstem CNS sites and cauda/extraneural retroperitoneal-paraspinal locations, and does not arise in endocrine glands (adrenal, parathyroid, pituitary, pineal, carotid body, paraganglia).
